concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying the party applying in a specified patent or trademark matter.
concepts.scopeNote: 35 USC 118; 37 CFR 1.42. This patent source supplies patent context only; trademark applicability requires separate authority evidence.

concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying a party to which rights are transferred by an assignment.
A contextual role identifying the practitioner recorded as representing a party in a specified matter.
concepts.scopeNote: 37 CFR 1.32; 37 CFR 2.17. This patent source supplies patent context only; trademark applicability requires separate authority evidence.

concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying a party designated as a client communication contact.
concepts.scopeNote: Repository definition; this public authority provides procedural context, not a universal definition. Scope and supporting evidence are consumer-owned.

concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying the designated recipient or sender of matter correspondence.
A contextual role identifying the official examining a specified application or proceeding.
A contextual role attributing conception of a specified invention to a natural person on supporting evidence.
A contextual role identifying a party receiving permission under a specified licence.
concepts.scopeNote: Repository definition; this public authority provides procedural context, not a universal definition. Scope and supporting evidence are consumer-owned.

concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying a party granting permission under a specified licence.
concepts.scopeNote: Repository definition; this public authority provides procedural context, not a universal definition. Scope and supporting evidence are consumer-owned.

concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying a party holding rights in a specified asset.
concepts.scopeNote: 35 USC 261; 15 USC 1058. This patent source supplies patent context only; trademark applicability requires separate authority evidence.

concepts.definition: A contextual role identifying the party signing a specified document or submission.
